headline: Eid-e-Miladunnabi observed today across Bangladesh with religious solemnity
summary: The day commemorates the birth and death anniversary of Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), who was born in Makkah in 570 AD and passed away on the same day in 632 AD.
details: The holy Eid-e-Miladunnabi, marking the birth and death anniversary of Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), is being observed across Bangladesh today with due religious solemnity. The Prophet was born in Makkah in 570 AD on the 12th of Rabiul Awal, bringing divine blessings and a message of peace for mankind.
He passed away on the same day in 632 AD. The government has undertaken extensive national-level programmes to mark this national holiday.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued separate messages yesterday, extending greetings to Muslims worldwide. The President also inaugurated the Islamic Foundation’s fortnight-long “Siratunnabi (PBUH) Programme” at the Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in Dhaka yesterday evening.

As part of the national programme, the national flag will be hoisted today at all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, private establishments, and armed forces installations. Special prayers are being offered at mosques nationwide, including the Bangladesh Secretariat Mosque, while Bangladesh missions abroad are also observing the day.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Canada imposes 15-50% counter-tariffs on US goods]], escalating trade war
headline: Canada imposes 15-50% counter-tariffs on US goods, escalating trade war
summary: Ottawa's retaliation, effective September 8, matches US duties on Canadian products and impacts industries like steel, dairy, and electronics. This move intensifies the trade dispute between the historically close allies.
details: Canada has announced counter-tariffs on US goods, ranging from 15 percent to 50 percent, in a significant escalation of the trade war between the historically close allies. This move comes after US President Trump imposed 50-percent duties on Canadian products.

Ottawa's retaliation is set to take effect on September 8, a timeframe previously outlined by Prime Minister Mark Carney. Officials stated that Canada's duties will directly match the US levels, impacting key industries such as steel, dairy, and electronics.

In addition to the tariffs, the Canadian government has also unveiled a substantial $5.4 billion (CA$7.5 billion) aid package. This fund is intended to support firms and workers affected by the ongoing trade dispute.

Canada's Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne remarked, "This is an unprecedented challenge imposed on Canada. But Canada will meet the moment." The US tariffs previously hit approximately $20 billion in Canadian goods, representing about 5.5 percent of its exports to the US, following a collapse in trade negotiations.

Under Canada's new plan, US steel and aluminum products, which were already subject to a 25-percent duty, will now face 50-percent tariffs. Goods like appliances, dairy products such as cheese, and certain steel and aluminum derivative products will incur 25-percent tariffs.

A smaller category, including electric equipment and tools, will see a 15-percent duty. The trade tensions are further complicated by Trump's pledge to double tariffs on Canadian autos next year, from 25 percent to 50 percent for non-US content.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford sharply criticized Trump's auto tariff threat, stating he could "kiss my ass" and warning of a potential electricity export surcharge. The escalating measures highlight the deepening rift in economic relations.
